{{short description|German chemist}}
'''Hildegard Hess''' (born 1920 in Berlin-Britz, died 23 July 2014) was a German chemist.{{refn|<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.institut-kirchhoff.de/|title=Institut Kirchhoff Berlin GmbH|last=GmbH|first=Institut Kirchhoff Berlin|date=2016|website=Institut Kirchhoff Berlin GmbH|language=de|access-date=2019-01-19}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.gdch.de/fileadmin/downloads/Netzwerk_und_Strukturen/Fachgruppen/AKCC/chemikerinnen_akcc.pdf|title=Chemikerinnen|website=www.gdch.de|access-date=2019-01-12}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://trauer.tagesspiegel.de/traueranzeige/hildegard-hess|title=Gedenkseite von Hildegard Hess|website=trauer.tagesspiegel.de|language=de|access-date=2019-01-19}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|last=Boeck|first=Gisela|date=2003|title=Unabhängig ein Leben lang|journal=Nachrichten aus der Chemie|language=de|volume=51|issue=1|pages=67–68|doi=10.1002/nadc.20030510133|issn=1868-0054}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kunert‐Kirchhoff|first1=Jutta|last2=Kirchhoff|first2=Erhard|date=2014|title=Frau Dr. Hildegard Hess|journal=Lebensmittelchemie|language=en|volume=68|issue=5|pages=116|doi=10.1002/lemi.201490043|issn=1521-3811}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite journal|last=Johnson|first=Jeffrey A.|date=1998-12-01|title=German women in chemistry, 1925–1945 (part II)|journal=NTM International Journal of History & Ethics of Natural Sciences, Technology & Medicine|language=en|volume=6|issue=1|pages=65–90|doi=10.1007/BF02914207|pmid=27518333|s2cid=33178544|issn=1420-9144}}</ref>}} She was the first woman to become a Handelschemiker (professional consultant industrial chemist) and to direct an independent testing laboratory in Berlin, if not in all of Germany.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":3" />

== Life ==
Hess was born in Berlin-Britz.<ref name=":0" /> Her father, Ludwig Hess, was the director of a Riedel de Haën factory.<ref name=":0" /> Her mother, Hertha Hess, was a trained nurse.<ref name=":0" /> Her parents sent Hess to a monastery school from which she graduated in 1939.<ref name=":0" /> This school was closed by the National Socialists a year later.<ref name=":0" /> She began her studies at the [[Friedrich-Wilhelm University]] in Berlin,<ref name=":0" /> and later transferred to the [[Albert Ludwig University of Freiburg]].<ref name=":0" /> Among her professors were [[Georg Wittig]] and [[Hermann Staudinger]].<ref name=":0" /> In 1944, Hess completed her training at the Reichsanstalt für Lebensmittel und Arzneimittelchemie in Berlin and became a state-certified [[food chemist]], before joining the independent testing laboratory of her father, which he took over in 1931.<ref name=":0" /> Such analytical laboratories for food monitoring supplemented the state institutions.<ref name=":0" />  While working at her father's institute, Hess simultaneously studied for her doctorate with [[Josef Schormüller]] at the Institute of Food Chemistry of [[Technische Universität Berlin]],<ref name=":2" /> which she finished in 1953.<ref name=":2" /> In 1954, she became the first publicly appointed female Handelschemiker (professional consultant industrial chemist) in Berlin.<ref name=":0" /> After her father's death in 1956, she took over his laboratory and continued his work until 1986.<ref name=":0" /> In addition to her work as a self-employed chemist, Hess taught as a lecturer.<ref name=":0" /> She conducted courses for food retailers in [[health food store]]s and from 1955 to 1965, taught [[nutritional science]] for students at [[Technische Universität Berlin]].<ref name=":0" /> [[Máire MacSwiney Brugha|Maire MacSwiney Brugha]] probably regarded her as a friend.<ref>{{Cite book|title=History's daughter : a memoir from the only child of Terence MacSwiney|last=Brugha|first=Máire MacSwiney|publisher=The O'Brien Press|year=2014|isbn=9781847176233|location=Dublin|oclc=872992030}}</ref>
